_note: Every technology in the game: its name, what KIND it is and what it unlocks or moves, its price and clock, and its slot on its tome page with what it needs before it — plus each book's BANDS and what each one asks for in revealed cells. What a card SAYS is generated from its unlocks or effects (src/sim/techProse.ts); only a mechanic, whose effect is code, carries a written description. Authored in ?dev=tree (Docs/tech-tree-editor.md) — the Technologies and Eras sheets are gone, and the districts, units and harvest sources no longer name their own gate. Ordered by tome, then down the page, then left to right.

Apprenticeships.name: Apprenticeships
Apprenticeships.description: Masters and their apprentices — the Townhall trains two villagers at once.

LandSurvey.name: Land Survey
LandSurvey.description: Chains and stakes — every building works one cell farther out.

Roadworks.name: Roadworks
Roadworks.description: Paved ways — every worker walks a quarter faster.

FieldMedicine.name: Field Medicine
FieldMedicine.description: Bandages and splints — the party recovers some HP between depths.

Scouting.name: Scouting
Scouting.description: Eyes ahead — a ruin shows its threat before you launch.

Siegecraft.name: Siegecraft
Siegecraft.description: Ladders and rams — a party can clear a defended landmark.

Veterancy.name: Veterancy
Veterancy.description: Hard-won experience — heroes gain levels from delving.

Tactics.name: Tactics
Tactics.description: Reading the ground — a bad matchup costs a tenth less.

Conquest.name: Conquest
Conquest.description: Held ground — every cleared ruin teaches you more, hour by hour.

Salvage.name: Salvage
Salvage.description: Pick over the losses — a failed depth costs 35% of the haul, not half.

Vanguard.name: Vanguard
Vanguard.description: Known ground — the first depth of a ruin you have cleared resolves at once.

Standards.name: Standards
Standards.description: Regimental colours — the army cap rises with every hall level.

WarbandIV.name: Warband IV
WarbandIV.description: Marching order. Each banner raised lets the four halls train a rank higher, and a bigger hall is a bigger army.

Invocation.name: Invocation
Invocation.description: Spoken twice — a relic's active gains a second charge.

Meditation.name: Meditation
Meditation.description: Stillness — the kingdom holds 30 more Mana.

LeyReading.name: Ley Reading
LeyReading.description: Reading the lines — a landmark shows what it grants before you pay.

Scrying.name: Scrying
Scrying.description: Seeing into stone — a ruin shows its tier before you commit a party.

FrugalRites.name: Frugal Rites
FrugalRites.description: Economy of gesture — some taps cost no Mana.

LeyLines.name: Ley Lines
LeyLines.description: The land's own current — a district beside the Sanctum produces a tenth more.

Lorekeeping.name: Lorekeeping
Lorekeeping.description: Records of the deep — ruins give up more of what they hold.

ScalingTools.name: Scaling Tools
ScalingTools.description: Ropes and pitons — the surveyors reach the high ground. Pitons, Vigils and Farsight build on it.

Wayshrines.name: Wayshrines
Wayshrines.description: Shrines on the road — a cleared defended landmark becomes claimable.

RitualCasting.name: Ritual Casting
RitualCasting.description: Rites over the roof — a relic's active can target a building.

LeyStorm.name: Ley Storm
LeyStorm.description: Once a day — a kingdom-wide surge of production for a while.

SanctifiedRuins.name: Sanctified Ruins
SanctifiedRuins.description: Consecrated ground — a cleared ruin's Knowledge drip doubles.

AttunementIV.name: Attunement IV
AttunementIV.description: Communion with the land. Each degree of it lets the Sanctum hold a level more, and the Sanctum is where Mana comes from.
